flakes.test: src/companions.spec.tsx > Switching views > opens a plan's editor as it was left
flakes.signature: AssertionError: expected .+ to be
flakes.cause: Two causes, both fixed. First (#232), the spec: it scrolled the pane to line 200 right after typing at the top of a restored one, and typing scrolls the caret into view in the editor's next measure, which on a slow frame came after the spec's scroll and put the pane back at the top, so its saved place was the first line; the spec now waits two frames after typing. Second, the app: a plan restored in Canvas, which scales the pane in, aimed at its saved line from the live zoom while CodeMirror's line heights were still at its last measured scale, as a transform alone doesn't make it measure; on a busy page the restore settled on a wrong line (the Steps heading) before the editor measured again. The restore now asks for a measure and waits while the editor's scale lags the pane's (libraries/viewers markdown/scroll.ts).

flakes.test: src/e2e/escape-race.e2e.ts > Antigravity > reads a turn that finished despite the Escape as completed with its reply, and one the Escape stopped as interrupted
flakes.signature: input box holds text already: a draft the prompt would merge into
flakes.cause: A freshly started Antigravity on Windows showed the runner screen's own mode-2026 report (a DECRQM reply with its ESC dropped, '[[?2026;2$y') as typed text in its input box, there at the first read after the banner and still there 3 s later (the run's trace), so that terminal's first prompt was refused as a draft. The runner's headless screen writes the reply to the pty (libraries/terminal host/terminal.ts, screen.onData). That the reply is the cause is inferred from the match, not probed on Windows ConPTY; fixing it is a product choice (not answering mode queries for Antigravity, or holding replies until its input is in VT mode) that needs a Windows probe. The signature is the generic draft refusal, which the log shows without the box's text, so a real regression of this test (an Escape leaving text in the box) reads as this flake once; its second failure is triaged.

flakes.test: src/pty/native.test.ts > installed native PTY dependency > starts a child and delivers its final output without hiding native startup errors

flakes.cause: Suspected, not reproduced on Linux (40 spawns each with the event loop stalled 0, 100 and 400 ms all delivered): node-pty reported the child's exit (code 0) without its output on macOS. Either node-pty's unixTerminal.js destroyed the pty socket 200 ms (DESTROY_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_MS) after the native exit callback, before the master was read, or macOS dropped the pending output when the last slave fd closed. Both are inside node-pty or the kernel; the repo's node-pty patch touches only Windows files.

flakes.test: src/e2e/chat.e2e.ts > Antigravity > runs a ! command from the chat, the same command again, and a multi-line one
flakes.signature: can't reach ready: timed out after \d+ ms\. \w+: unbound[\s\S]*error entering raw mode: input/output error
flakes.cause: Antigravity's CLI exited at startup with "CLI error: error entering raw mode: input/output error", right after the macOS shell (bash 3.2) reported "child setpgid (N to N): Operation not permitted", so the terminal never bound an agent. Suspected: a race in which the CLI leaves bash's process group (as by setsid) before bash puts it in its own, so it isn't in the terminal's foreground group and its tcsetattr fails with EIO. Seen once, on macOS; not reproduced on Linux.

flakes.signature: page\.evaluate: WireError: Could not connect\.|could not reach the packaged runner after \d+ ms
flakes.cause: Not a test: the packaged smoke check's first connection to the runner fails on Windows now and then. Both times it gave up 14 to 16 s after the app's launch, the launch plus the first connection's 10 s handshake limit, where a passing run reaches the shell in under 3 s; so the packaged runner sometimes takes over 10 s to start answering on a fresh Windows runner (suspected: a cold start, as Defender scanning the new package). The same limit applies to the app's own first connection. The smoke check now reports the failure's cause and how long it took, which the next occurrence will settle.

flakes.test: src/engines/server.test.ts > a server > starts again on another port when something takes the one it was given
flakes.signature: AssertionError: expected 2 to be 3
flakes.cause: The test's own: of the three ports it expects to be different, two were the same. Its first two starts only say their port is taken and exit (losesPort), holding no socket, on purpose, so as not to race other test workers for free ports. The server's next pick (freePort in backend/runner/src/engines/server.ts: bind port 0, then close) can then get the same port back from the OS. The server promises no more: a port another process really holds can't be picked again while it's held. A fix would hold each lost port in the test, bringing back the race its comment avoids, or let the test choose the ports.

flakes.test: src/messaging/messaging.test.ts > delivery through hooks > delivers several messages together, up to 8 KB as printed, the rest at the next hook

flakes.test: src/process-windows.spec.tsx > process windows > presents claude in its window with input and controls in every layout
flakes.signature: AssertionError: expected false to be true|the view never settled in \d+ looks
flakes.cause: The spec helper's wait for the view to settle (layoutSettled, which every openWorkspace ends with) polled with a 5 s timeout, and a file's first spec, mounting the demo's terminals cold on a loaded Windows runner, drew no second frame within it, though the view had already stopped moving. Reproduced locally with Chromium's CPU throttled 30x: 5 of 11 runs failed, each after one frame drawn, and a 10 s timeout still failed 3 of 8. The wait now counts its looks and checks the time only once a frame is drawn, leaving a page that never draws again to the test's timeout (0 of 10 failed at 30x).
